findings.description: move_card loads the card and only calls _require_editor on to_board_id. The actor's role on the card's current board is never checked. Any user who is an editor on some board of their own can move another board's card into it, which takes the card (and its content) out of a board they may have no access to, or only viewer access. It also lets them read the card via the returned object.
findings.suggestion: Call self._require_editor(card.board_id, actor_id) for the source board before any mutation, in addition to the target check.
findings.title: Move checks editor rights only on the target board, not the source board

findings.description: archive_card calls detach and then sets archived=True, but leaves card.position unchanged. Archived cards are excluded from cards_in_column, so the stale position isn't compacted afterwards. Meanwhile edit_card and view_card still operate on archived cards without any check, so archived cards remain editable. This is inconsistent with move_card, which rejects archived cards.
findings.suggestion: Reject or explicitly allow edits on archived cards consistently, and reset position when archiving.
findings.title: Archived card keeps a stale position and unarchive/other paths are inconsistent

findings.description: On a move within the same column, detach decrements positions of lower cards, but the card keeps its old position and is excluded from `others` in insert, so it works. However, when moving a card to a different board, detach uses card.board_id before reassigning, which is correct. The stale card.position is passed over; the real issue is that `position > len(others)` clamps but detach-then-insert on the same column with position equal to len(others) is fine. Low risk.
findings.title: Moving within the same column: detach then insert miscounts position
